rationale: Both candidates correctly reconstruct the ground-truth concern: an earlier commit added trust_remote_code (breaking kernels 0.13.x), commit 9947f414 dropped it, but the PR description still advertises the removed kwarg — X covers this concisely in point 6, Y covers it with more forensic commit tracing but restates it three near-identical times. Both add solid additional grounded findings (sticky version-fallback caching due to the process-wide cache, missing test coverage for the new cache/fallback path, the likely-unrelated NPU CI failure), and Y contributes a couple of sharper unique catches (FA3 path is never actually exercised even on hardware-gated tests, lock blocks unrelated repos). However Y's 'Validated' section and findings are heavily padded with near-duplicate restatements of the same 4-5 facts, which is pure verbosity that shouldn't be rewarded and hurts real-world usefulness, whereas X delivers comparable rigor (including an execution-verified claim) in a tight, clearly actionable structure.
